claims.claimText: UT's education PDF requires students to disclose AI use in an appendix when AI is used for an assignment, and states that unconsented and unacknowledged AI use should be considered academic misconduct.

evidence.evidenceSnippet: It is required that students mention the use of AI. Therefore, when any form of AI is used, the use of these tools should be included in the appendix... Students using AI, without the explicit consent of the instructor and acknowledgement of the tool in an appendix, should therefore be considered to have committed academic misconduct.
evidence.evidenceSnippetDisplay: UT requires AI use disclosure in an appendix and treats unconsented, unacknowledged AI use as academic misconduct.

claims.claimText: UT's AI dossier tells users not to include personal, student, research, confidential, or sensitive data in public AI tools.

evidence.evidenceSnippet: How should I handle data when using AI tools? Always assume your input may be stored externally. Never include personal data, student details, research data or confidential material in public AI tools.
evidence.evidenceSnippetDisplay: UT warns users not to put personal, student, research, or confidential data into public AI tools.
evidence.snippetLocation: FAQ by topic > IT, Security & legal

claims.claimText: UT's education PDF tells teachers that each assignment or group of assignments should make clear whether students may use AI and whether restrictions apply.

evidence.evidenceSnippet: With every assignment or group of assignments it should be clear if students are allowed to use AI and whether this is with restrictions. See below for options.
evidence.evidenceSnippetDisplay: UT tells teachers to make assignment-level AI permissions and restrictions clear.

claims.claimText: The University of Twente Executive Board has adopted an AI statement that frames AI use as a shared, responsible practice across education, research, and operations.

evidence.evidenceSnippet: The Executive Board of the University of Twente has adopted a statement on artificial intelligence (AI). In this statement, the university highlights the importance of a shared and responsible use of AI within education, research, and operations.
evidence.evidenceSnippetDisplay: UT says its Executive Board adopted an AI statement emphasizing shared and responsible AI use in education, research, and operations.

claims.claimText: For student assignments and theses, UT's AI dossier says AI tool use depends on the course and on policies set by the programme or lecturer.

evidence.evidenceSnippet: Can students use AI tools for assignments or theses? That depends on the course. Each programme or lecturer may have their own policy. When in doubt, ask your lecturer. Always use AI transparently and responsibly.
evidence.evidenceSnippetDisplay: Student AI use for assignments or theses depends on the course, programme, or lecturer policy.

claims.claimText: UT's AI dossier says the university is developing an AI Compliance Framework and instructs staff and researchers to report AI applications via the AI Office for appropriate measures under the AI Act.

evidence.evidenceSnippet: UT is developing an AI Compliance Framework to provide guidance on legal and regulatory matters, such as the European AI Act... Always report your AI application via the AI Office to ensure that the appropriate measures can be taken in line with the AI Act.
evidence.evidenceSnippetDisplay: UT is developing an AI Compliance Framework and directs AI applications to the AI Office for AI Act-related measures.
evidence.snippetLocation: AI & IT security > AI Compliance Framework

claims.claimText: UT's AI dossier says users should seek Contract Management approval before accepting licence agreements for new AI applications or paid AI tools that may bind the university.

evidence.evidenceSnippet: Before using any new application or tool, please note that, according to the Use of Personal Applications Policy, it is not permitted to accept license agreements that are binding for the university without prior approval. This applies to both paid and unpaid licenses.
evidence.evidenceSnippetDisplay: UT says licence agreements binding the university need prior approval, including paid and unpaid licences.

claims.claimText: UT's AI and assessment guidance warns that AI detection software has limits and may raise privacy, confidentiality, and trustworthiness issues.

evidence.evidenceSnippet: There are AI detection software, but in general, they have their limits and are not very reliable. There are also privacy, confidentiality, and other issues involved if the work of students or others is put in a system to check.
evidence.evidenceSnippetDisplay: UT warns teachers that AI detection software is limited and may raise privacy or confidentiality issues.
